key_insight: Inference-Time Argumentation (ITA) combines neural evidence retrieval with a formal, trainable symbolic argumentation layer to produce ternary (true / false / uncertain) claim verification decisions and faithful, human-interpretable explanations at inference time.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable binary claim verification under incomplete or conflicting evidence by enabling uncertainty-aware (ternary) verdicts and providing faithful, structured explanations that show how supporting and opposing evidence were weighed.
method: Neural evidence modules retrieve and score candidate premises and counterpremises from text at inference time.
A symbolic argumentation engine constructs argument graphs (supporting vs. attacking arguments) and applies formal argumentation semantics to produce accept/reject/undecided verdicts.
The pipeline is trainable end-to-end or via modular objectives so argument scoring and selection align with final ternary decisions and explanation fidelity.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical, interpretable approach for high-stakes fact-checking and decision-making systems where uncertainty must be reported and the rationale must be auditable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: neural retriever/reader → argument graph builder → argumentation semantics → ternary verdict + explanation
Example argumentation graph: nodes for premises, support/attack edges, highlighted accepted arguments leading to the verdict
Ternary verdict gauge: true / uncertain / false with calibration/confidence bars
Side-by-side explanation panel: original claim, top supporting and attacking evidence snippets, concise justification sentence
paper_authors: Gabriel Freedman, Adam Dejl, Adam Gould,  Mansi, Lihu Chen
